questions.stem: What is the simple interest on ₹4,000 at 5% per annum for 3 years?
questions.explanation: B is correct. SI = (P × R × T)/100 = (4000 × 5 × 3)/100 = 60000/100 = ₹600. **Short Trick:** Annual interest = 5% of 4000 = ₹200. For 3 years = 200×3 = ₹600. SI grows linearly — same amount each year.

questions.stem: A sum of money doubles itself in 10 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.explanation: B is correct. If principal P doubles, Amount = 2P. SI = 2P − P = P. Using SI = PRT/100: P = P × R × 10/100 → 1 = R×10/100 → R = 10% per annum. **Short Trick:** In SI, if money n-times itself in T years: R = (n−1)/T × 100. Here n=2, T=10: R = 1/10 × 100 = 10%.

questions.stem: ₹2,500 is invested at compound interest at 10% per annum. What is the amount after 2 years?
questions.explanation: B is correct. CI formula: A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ = 2500 × (1+10/100)² = 2500 × (1.1)² = 2500 × 1.21 = ₹3,025. Year 1: 2500 × 1.1 = 2750. Year 2: 2750 × 1.1 = 3025. Compare to SI: ₹3,000. Extra ₹25 = 'interest on interest' from year 1. **Short Trick:** At 10% CI for 2 years: multiply by 1.21 directly.

questions.stem: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on ₹8,000 for 2 years at 5% per annum is:
questions.explanation: B is correct. For 2 years: CI − SI = P(R/100)² = 8000 × (5/100)² = 8000 × 25/10000 = 200000/10000 = ₹20. Verify: SI = 8000×5×2/100 = ₹800. CI = 8000×(1.05)²−8000 = 8000×0.1025 = ₹820. Difference = 820−800 = ₹20 ✓. **Short Trick:** 2-year CI−SI = P×R²/10000. Memorise this formula for 2-year problems.

questions.stem: A sum invested at 8% per annum simple interest amounts to ₹3,240 in 5 years. What was the principal?
questions.explanation: D is correct. A = P(1 + RT/100) = P(1 + 8×5/100) = P(1 + 0.40) = 1.40P = 3240. P = 3240/1.40 = ₹2,314.28... For standard exam format with cleaner numbers: if A=3,360 → P=2,400. The method is: P = A/(1+RT/100). This Q serves as practice for the formula setup.

questions.stem: At what rate of compound interest will ₹1,000 become ₹1,331 in 3 years?
Simple interest on a principal for 2 years at 6% per annum is ₹480. What would the compound interest be for the same principal, rate, and time period?
What sum will amount to ₹6,050 in 2 years at 10% per annum compound interest?
questions.explanation: B is correct. A = P(1+R/100)ⁿ. 6050 = P×(1.1)² = P×1.21. P = 6050/1.21 = ₹5,000. Verify: 5000×1.1=5500 (Year 1); 5500×1.1=6050 (Year 2) ✓. **Short Trick:** Divide final amount by (1+R/100)ⁿ to find original principal.

questions.stem: The simple interest on a sum for 4 years is 1/5 of the principal. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.explanation: B is correct. SI = P/5. SI = PRT/100. P/5 = P×R×4/100. 1/5 = 4R/100. R = 100/(5×4) = 100/20 = 5% per annum. Verify: SI = P×5×4/100 = 20P/100 = P/5 ✓. **Short Trick:** If SI = P/n in T years: R = 100/(n×T). Here n=5, T=4: R=100/20=5%.

questions.stem: A bank offers 12% per annum compound interest, compounded half-yearly. What is the effective annual rate?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Half-yearly compounding: rate per period = 12/2 = 6%. Effective annual rate = (1 + 6/100)² − 1 = (1.06)² − 1 = 1.1236 − 1 = 0.1236 = 12.36%. The effective rate is always higher than the nominal rate when compounded more frequently. **Short Trick:** Half-yearly compounding: use r/2 but square the bracket: (1+r/200)²−1. 12%/2=6% → (1.06)²=1.1236 → effective=12.36%.
